tweet.text:
i place near zero probability that the labs will agree on a single "third-party safety evaluator" who is:

1) competent enough to actually do frontier evals (that isn't repackaging existing evals)

2) is not financially tied to an existing lab

3) will actually have the backbone to speak up when things "go wrong"
